_comment: Presentation only: the words the site shows. No facts about people live here — those are in data/. Every translatable value is an object keyed by language code, so a missing translation is visible in the diff rather than in the browser; the validator refuses a build where one is absent. `kinship` is keyed by language at the top instead, because the shape of the vocabulary is not the same in both: English stacks one prefix (great-great-) where Dutch has a different word for each of the first steps (over-, betover-).

footer.en: A living draft. Documented lines rest on Belgian civil and parish records, reached through the state archives and the member trees credited in the sources list; the rest is family knowledge, marked as such. Living individuals were not researched beyond what the family volunteered.
footer.nl: Een levend concept. De gedocumenteerde lijnen berusten op Belgische akten van de burgerlijke stand en parochieregisters, geraadpleegd via het rijksarchief en de ledenstambomen die in de bronnenlijst vermeld staan; de rest is familiekennis, en staat als zodanig aangeduid. Naar levende personen is niet verder gezocht dan wat de familie zelf heeft verteld.

kinship._comment: The vocabulary `relationBetween` builds a relation out of. Each entry is f/m/n — the neutral form is what someone whose sex no record states gets, because guessing it from a forename would be inventing a fact. A prefix list is read: index 0 for no step, then one entry per step, and the last entry is the template for everything beyond them. English stacks `great-` forever; Dutch has over-, betover-, and then needs a count too.
